sectors.trend: Mixed: gold miners under pressure from lower spot gold and rising real yields; coal names benefit from 'lucky country' boom; exploration sector sees multiple positive WA/Qld hits (King River, Moonlight, McLaren, Larvotto). MIN.AX de-risked post-ASIC clearance.
sectors.implications: Rotate from gold into coal and base metals. Exploration names (MIN.AX, VGC.AX) offer speculative upside. BHP.AX, BRL.AX benefit from coal strength. Gold miners (GWN.AX, NLA.AX) face near-term headwinds.

sectors.trend: Rate-hike expectations support net interest margins for CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX, but property credit stress (investor credit crash, Bathla warning) raises NPL concerns. Housing market fragility is a structural risk.
sectors.implications: Banks benefit from higher RBA cash rate but face elevated credit risk in property lending. Monitor NAB.AX and ANZ.AX for property exposure. Defensive positioning in CBA.AX preferred.

sectors.trend: Oil prices jump on Middle East tensions; diesel shock described as 'forever now'. Wind farm drought in Australia being addressed by Danish entrant. Smart money favouring operators over megawatts.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WES.AX, and oil-exposed names benefit from higher crude. Renewable energy names (SOL.AX, LEM.AX) see catalyst from Danish wind farm entry. Diesel cost inflation pressures transport and logistics.

sectors.trend: CSL.AX signs Trump administration deal to slash medicine prices — significant margin compression risk. HQY shows health savings engine momentum. Weight-loss drug demand surging in Australia.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX faces pricing headwinds from US deal; monitor margin guidance. Domestic healthcare (SGH.AX, IAG.AX) may benefit from weight-loss drug demand. Defensive healthcare still attractive but CSL.AX specifically under pressure.

sectors.trend: Qantas (QAN.AX) ground crew strike vote creates operational risk. Jetstar (JQZ.AX) launches Western Sydney Airport route. Per capita recession fears persist. 'Dupe' brands and EV uptake accelerating.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces near-term disruption risk from strike vote. JQZ.AX benefits from WSA expansion. Consumer staples (WES.AX, CCL.AX) offer defensive value amid per capita recession concerns.

sectors.trend: Sydney house price crash gaining global attention. Property investor credit growth crashes post-budget tax changes. Renter respite emerging. Negative gearing reform fails to ignite. Bathla developer near collapse.
sectors.implications: Property REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX) face valuation pressure. Residential REITs under stress. Monitor for further developer defaults. Renter-friendly policy shift may support long-term rental demand.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure over 1–3 months as oil-driven inflation keeps RBA on a hawkish path, bond yields stay elevated, and property credit stress persists. Gold miners face headwinds from lower spot gold. Coal and banks are relative outperformers. Qantas strike risk adds volatility. Expect ^AXJO to trade in a range with downside bias until RBA signals pause.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook is cautiously constructive if RBA pivots and oil stabilises. Coal boom, exploration pipeline, and renewable energy build-out support materials and energy sectors. CSL.AX pricing deal is a structural headwind but Australian healthcare demand (weight-loss drugs, ageing population) provides offset. Property sector needs 12+ months to stabilise post-tax changes. Per capita recession risk is the key wildcard.
